gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each brand charges per added Wh when you expand later (OUPES B2 $0.28/Wh, EcoFlow DELTA 3 extra battery $0.38/Wh, Jackery Battery Pack 2000 Plus v2 $0.49/Wh). None states that a DELTA 3 plus its 1,024 Wh extra battery ($579 + $388 = $967 for 2,048 Wh) costs $88 more than EcoFlow's own 2,048 Wh DELTA 3 Max listing at $879 today.
standout_why: StormWatts (cited) computes cost-to-2-kWh for the DELTA 3 Plus only: $719 + $389 = $1,108, $0.54/Wh, add-on $0.38/Wh, using an October 10 base price. It doesn't price any other brand's pack. WattHourLab (cited) has no prices; it gives only 48.3 Wh/lb for the EcoFlow pack. Off Grid Field Guide (cited) gives Wh/lb but no prices. BatteryRank (cited) has no prices, weights or $/Wh. None compares cost per added Wh across EcoFlow, OUPES and Jackery. None checks whether 'start at 1 kWh, add a battery later' costs more than buying 2 kWh up front.
decides: This confirms the EcoFlow DELTA 3 as the cheapest way to start at 1 kWh with a 1 kWh step later ($579 now, $388 later). It also adds a caveat: if the shopper already knows they want 2 kWh, the 2 kWh DELTA 3 Max listing ($879) costs less than DELTA 3 + extra battery ($967). For growing past 2 kWh, OUPES Mega 1 + B2 has the lowest system cost per Wh ($0.42/Wh at 3,072 Wh) and the cheapest added Wh ($0.28). Jackery HomePower 1000 Plus v2 costs the most per added Wh ($0.49), and its smallest step is 2,048 Wh.
